issues.claim: Sources line: "https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data/OEUS340000000000047218113 — NJ first-line-supervisor median, May 2025" (supports the $63.41/hour used in section 3)
issues.problem: Wrong series cited. Opening that URL myself returns year 2025 value 76600, which is occupation 47-2181 (Roofers, NJ), not 47-1011. The first-line-supervisor series is OEUS340000000000047101113 and returns 105510 — the figure the audit body actually uses. The $63.41 rate is arithmetically right for $105,510, but the citation attached to it does not support it, and the same swapped URL was carried into analysis.json.
issues.fix: Replace that source URL with https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data/OEUS340000000000047101113 (returns 105510, 2025) and label it "NJ first-line supervisors of construction trades (47-1011)". Keep OEUS340000000000047218113 only if roofers ($76,600) are being cited for something.

issues.claim: Impact line, section 2: "about 117–364 staff hours a year (… 780–1,560 inquiries x 0.25–0.33 h each x 60–70% handled) = about $3,356–$10,443 a year"; prep note "1,560 x 0.33 x 70% = 364 h"
issues.problem: The stated top of the range does not follow from the stated inputs. 1,560 x 0.33 x 0.70 = 360.36 h, i.e. ~360 h and ~$10,339 at $28.69/h, not 364 h and $10,443. A reader who redoes the multiplication finds the top of the range overstated by about 1%. (364 h is only reachable if handling time is 20 minutes = 0.333 h.) The low end is correct: 780 x 0.25 x 0.60 = 117 h and $3,356.
issues.fix: Either state 0.33 h as 20 minutes / one-third hour and derive 364 h explicitly, or change the top to 360 h and about $10,339. Add the rounded figures actually used, as the other two sections do.

issues.claim: Prep note: "Hours are the inline products, rounded down: 12 x 0.25 x 100% = 3 h and 24 x 0.33 x 100% = 8 h"
issues.problem: Internal inconsistency. 24 x 0.33 = 7.92, which is 7 h if rounded down; 8 h is a round-up. The audit text itself ("about 3–8 staff hours") is defensible, but the stated rounding rule is not what was applied.
issues.fix: Reword to "rounded to the nearest hour" and note the effect: 7.92 → 8 h, so the top figure ($229) is a slight overstatement of 7.92 x $28.69 ≈ $227.

issues.claim: Section 2, "Now": intake is one number, "with no form, chat or booking visible"
issues.problem: Overstated. The ProvenExpert profile the audit cites offers a public message form ("Your message to Biondo Contracting": name, email, phone, plus a "Callback request" checkbox and an "Arrange an appointment" link). It is not a quote form and its handling is unknown, but the audit should not tell the owner there is no form at all when one exists on a listing it names two lines later.
issues.fix: Narrow to: no quote form, chat or booking exists on the business's own website (the domain serves spam); the only non-phone channel is a generic message box on the ProvenExpert listing, which we could not confirm anyone reads.

issues.claim: "Suggested first step: A 20-minute walkthrough at your Monroe address (call (732) 257-2926 first; we have not confirmed it is staffed)" and the walk-in opener
issues.problem: Not a factual error — the address is publicly listed as the business address on Google and ProvenExpert, and the audit is honest that staffing is unconfirmed. But 38 Spotswood Ave may be a home/shopfront, and the only route offered is an unannounced walk-in at an address the audit itself says may be unstaffed.
issues.fix: Keep the call-first hedging and add a line to the prep notes: if the call is unanswered and the address looks residential, send the email instead of walking up. Do not present the address as a confirmed office.
